messages.subject: Re: Now what am I doing?
parts:
Barry:

I'll dismiss the data appearance for the moment, and concentrate on your
last question: why is your estimated density smaller than the naive
density of individuals you encountered? The reason for this is the area
over which your web is sampling animals is larger than simply the area
of the web.

Regarding the specification of survey effort by trap night. I believe
you are interested in estimating a single density estimate pertinent to
your sampling period that consists of 4(?) nights. You are not trying
to produce distinct estimates for each night. Hence, I don't believe
there is a reason for explicit description of trap nights in your
analysis. You will use first-captures from all sampling occasions
combined to produce your estimate of density.

messages.subject: Re: Now what am I doing?
parts:
Barry:

I think we're making progress. You bin your data (because your traps
exist only at a fixed number of distances from the centre of the plot);
because on say Tuesday you caught 4 individuals in the 3rd ring of traps
has *nothing to do* with the concept these 4 individuals were travelling
together (they may well have been at 12-3-6-9 o'clock on the spokes of
the web, many metres distant from one another). The amount of effort
you allocated to a web is a single value, not many. You are exactly
correct you are not dealing with clustered (or grouped) data [a
biological concept of the animals] but you are dealing with grouped data
[a consequence of the manner in which the sampling design (web) was
devised]. It is important to keep the distinction between the two quite
clear.

Barry Rosenbaum wrote:

> >Well,
> >
> >This may be the crux of my misunderstanding. I understand about the
> >combining of all first captures at a particular ring for the night and
> >a sampling effort of 1. This is what I did originally. But I assumed
> >that a grouping like that must be a cluster of catches at that
> >distance. To clarify then, I need to combine the data for a
> >particular ring distance but not treat it as a cluster.
> >
> >I do understand your point about the difference in data between naive
> >data and estimated data. The density I sent you was for an area of
> >3.44 ha (105m radius) instead of 3.14 ha (100m). Still quite a
> >difference.
